messages:
sara chen: @here Pager: high GPU queue growth for customer-vpc-42. Observed continuous enqueueing for 15m, GPU pool 'pv-gpu-eu-west' at 100% allocation, autoscaler failing to provision new nodes. Getting node creation errors: quota/timeout. Customer impacted.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-42 - Private cluster autoscale failure. Paging oncall.

miguel torres: I'm on it. Loading the queue metrics now. Which models are spiking?

sara chen: Looks like customer is hitting both embedding and chat endpoints, heavy short-chat workloads. model-serving: redwood/llama-70b-q4 -> many inflight requests. Prefix cache not helping because many unique contexts.

oncall-ml: I see 95% of queued requests are on model variant q4. Latency SLOs breached for that customer. ETA on node provisioning attempts?

ops-sre: Autoscaler logs show repeated failures creating instances in customer VPC: "AttachNetworkInterface: rate limit exceeded" then "InstanceProvisionTimeout after 6m". Also seeing taint mismatch on node bootstrap that caused kubelet to reject pods.

miguel torres: That taint mismatch — recent kubelet config change? Any recent kube-proxy or cloud-init changes?

ops-sre: No infra change in the last 48h for that cluster. But cloud provider bumped API throttling in that region earlier today (alerted to partners). Could be correlated.

nicole (CS): Customer reported timeouts ~ 11:02 UTC. They're seeing 503s. They're asking if this is a transient capacity issue or a config bug.

sara chen: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop routing new requests for customer-vpc-42 to the GPU pool (apply temporary rate limit / 429s). 2) fallback route for critical customers to CPU-backed smaller model variant (redwood/llama-70b-int8 -> redwood/llama-13b-int8?). 3) kick infra to manually provision emergency nodes with elevated quota. 4) coordinate with CS to notify customer with mitigation ETA.

oncall-ml: I'll implement model fallback tiering in routing policy now. Pushing canary that redirects 20% of traffic to 13b variant and 80% to queue with 30s timeout.

deploy-bot: Initiating routing change: route-update request submitted by oncall-ml. Change ID: r-2026-0314-99.

ops-sre: While you do that, I'm going to disable autoscaler for that pool and attempt manual node create. If cloud provider keeps rate limiting, we'll need to request quota bump / abuse exemption.

miguel torres: FYI the queue size is at 6.5k and growing ~300req/min. If manual nodes take >10m we'll hit customer SLA window. Prioritize emergency nodes.

infra-bot: Manual node create attempt started by ops-sre at 11:12 UTC.

ops-sre: Manual create failing with: "ENI allocation failed: insufficient subnet IPs". Looks like the customer's subnets are exhausted. This is a customer-side constraint — their VPC subnets don't have free IPs for new nodes.

nicole (CS): Reaching out to customer infrastructure contact now to request ephemeral IP pool expansion.

sara chen: Okay this is critical: autoscaler failing due to two independent issues: cloud API throttling + customer subnet IP exhaustion. Need immediate mitigation that doesn't require new nodes in that VPC.

oncall-ml: Rolling new policy: route all GPU-bound traffic for this customer to our cross-region fallback pool (hosted, different VPC) that has capacity but higher egress cost. This avoids relying on customer's subnets. Will mark traffic as 'best-effort' and throttle at 60% to avoid overloading fallback.

miguel torres: Will we violate data locality / compliance for this customer with cross-region fallback? They are in EU and have data residency requirement.

nicole (CS): Customer has allowed cross-region for non-sensitive workloads in their onboarding notes? I'm double-checking, but need explicit approval for production traffic.

sara chen: If we can't move traffic cross-region because of compliance, fallback options: 1) degrade quality to CPU variant in-situ (no new nodes), 2) apply short client-side backoff guidance (429 Retry-After), 3) partial feature flag to block heavy embedding endpoints. Which is fastest?

oncall-ml: CPU fallback is the fastest — we can route to existing CPU nodes inside the same VPC cluster that have spare capacity but lower throughput. Will apply model shrink policy to map 70b -> 13b. Executing now.

deploy-bot: Route-update executed: r-2026-0314-99 -> 100% fallback to CPU-tier for customer-vpc-42.

ops-sre: Confirming: CPU nodes accepted new pods. Queue drains slowly. Throughput per pod lower, but requests start returning 200s instead of 503.

miguel torres: Good. Start rate limiting to reduce burst until queue < 500. Set per-API key throttle to 20 qps and global customer token to 100 qps.

sara chen: Done. Config: 
```
rate_limit:
  customer: customer-vpc-42
  global_qps: 100
  per_key_qps: 20
  enforcement: proxy
```

ops-sre: CS update: customer acknowledged; they will expand subnet IPs but estimate 30-45m. They also raised a support ticket with cloud provider for API throttle.

nicole (CS): Customer appreciates quick mitigations. They're okay with temporary CPU fallback as long as latency and cost tradeoffs are clear. Asking for ETA on full GPU restoration.

sara chen: Current plan and next steps: 
- Short: CPU fallback + rate limits in place. Queue stabilizing, customer experiencing increased latency but success responses. (owner: oncall-ml, now)
- Mid: Coordinate with customer to expand subnet IPs; infra to re-enable autoscaler and perform controlled node scale once IPs are available. (owner: ops-sre, CS)
- Mid backup: If customer cannot expand IPs, propose private-hosted cross-region fallback if compliance allows. (owner: product/security)
- Postmortem: investigate autoscaler robustness to cloud API throttling and improve preflight checks for customer subnet capacity. (owner: eng-runtime)

miguel torres: Capturing actions for oncall handoff. I'll be taking the next shift in 20m. Handoff notes: CPU fallback applied, rate limits set, queue size 1.2k and dropping, customer working on expanding subnets, cloud provider ticket open.

oncall-ml: Leaving my notes: routing change id r-2026-0314-99, rollback plan if cpu nodes overload: revert route and enable strict 5xx shedding to preserve stability.

ops-sre: I'll continue trying manual node create periodically and will re-enable autoscaler once cloud API quotas look healthy. Also adding a preflight check to autoscaler: verify subnet IP availability before attempting node create. (temp patch in progress)

sara chen: Thanks team. Nicole, can you send the customer a short note summarizing mitigations and ETA? Include that we're monitoring and will update every 15m.

nicole (CS): Message sent at 11:35 UTC. Customer acknowledged and asked for a postmortem. I'll collect contact details for follow-up.

infra-bot: Update: cloud provider escalated the throttle issue to partner support, estimated 25m for resolution.

miguel torres: Queue is 420 and falling steadily. If we keep draining, we'll aim for full restore in ~40m after IP expansion. I'm handing over to @sara chen.

sara chen: Handoff accepted. I'll keep watch and collate logs for postmortem. Key lessons: (1) autoscaler should check subnet IPs and ENI quotas before scaling, (2) routing should have per-customer graceful fallback configured, (3) CS onboarding must capture subnet headroom requirements.

ops-sre: Filing incident report INC-2026-0314-42-action with the above actions and owners.

sara chen: Closing thread once customer confirms restored GPU capacity or we have final decision on cross-region fallback. For now, moving incident to 'mitigated' state. :white_check_mark:
